steps.title: Bordeaux
steps.body: Sémillon is Bordeaux's most planted white grape. It's blended with Sauvignon Blanc and a little Muscadelle in dry whites, from Entre-Deux-Mers to Pessac-Léognan, and in sweet wines, from Sauternes, Barsac, Loupiac and Cadillac. Bergerac and Monbazillac, nearby, also use it.

steps.title: Australia and beyond
steps.body: Australia is Sémillon's other great home: the Hunter Valley for unoaked, long-lived dry wines; Margaret River for Sémillon Sauvignon Blanc blends; the Barossa for richer, oaked styles. South Africa once had over 90% Sémillon in the 19th century; now old vines remain. Chile and Argentina grow it too.

steps.prompt: Match each place to its Sémillon.

steps.title: With Sauvignon
steps.body: Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc complement each other: Sémillon gives body, texture and ageing potential; Sauvignon gives aroma and acidity. In dry Bordeaux, the blend can age for decades. In Sauternes, Sémillon usually makes up about 80%, with Sauvignon adding freshness.

steps.prompt: What does Sémillon add to a blend with Sauvignon Blanc?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sémillon is Bordeaux's most planted white
Australia's Hunter and Margaret River are key homes
With Sauvignon, it balances body and freshness
